name: PEDIATRIC Wilms Tumor (Nephroblastoma): Regimen DD4A (vinCRIStine + Dactinomycin + DOXOrubicin), with Regimen EE4A (vinCRIStine + Dactinomycin) for lower-risk disease
histology: favorable-histology Wilms tumor (FHWT) is the DD4A/EE4A target; anaplastic histology (focal or diffuse) is unfavorable and is treated on distinct intensified regimens (M, I, UH-1, UH-2)
stage: DD4A: standard/higher-risk FHWT (e.g., stage III, or stage I-II with adverse molecular markers, or lung/extrapulmonary metastatic)

biomarkers.histology: favorable (FHWT) vs anaplastic (focal/diffuse); anaplasia is unfavorable and reassigns therapy
biomarkers.LOH_1p_16q: combined loss of heterozygosity at BOTH 1p and 16q is adverse and triggers intensification (switch/continue to DD4A, or to Regimen M)
biomarkers.gain_1q: 1q gain is associated with poorer outcome
biomarkers.LOH_LOI_11p15: 11p15 LOH or loss of imprinting may preclude therapy de-escalation
biomarkers.note: PEDIATRIC. Chemotherapy assignment is by histology (favorable vs anaplastic), stage, tumor weight, age, lung-metastasis response, and molecular markers. Combined LOH at 1p AND 16q, 1q gain, and 11p15 LOH/LOI are the actionable adverse molecular markers. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Wilms Tumor (Nephroblastoma) v1.2026, Initial/Final Risk Assessment for FHWT (WILMS-F, risk table lines 522 to 558) and updates on biomarker-directed intensification (lines 153, 184, 226 to 227). No endorsement implied.

treatmentSetting: neoadjuvant (unresectable tumor or when nephron-sparing surgery is indicated)
lineOfTherapy: first-line adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy for newly diagnosed Wilms tumor

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: favorable-histology Wilms tumor requiring adjuvant/neoadjuvant chemotherapy per risk group
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, Initial/Final Risk Assessment for FHWT (WILMS-F, lines 522 to 558); Chemotherapy Regimens (WILMS-G, lines 2027 to 2037)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: adjuvant chemotherapy started within 7 to 14 days of up-front nephrectomy, coordinated with radiation to avoid full-dose dactinomycin/doxorubicin during RT
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v1.2026, Principles of Systemic Therapy (line 2019 to 2021)

drugs.name: vinCRIStine

provenance.locator: Chemotherapy Regimens (WILMS-G): DD4A = 15 doses of vincristine over 24 weeks; EE4A = 13 doses of vincristine over 18 weeks (lines 2028 to 2029)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC. DD4A specifies 15 doses of vincristine over 24 weeks (EE4A: 13 doses over 18 weeks). The source prints dose COUNTS and total duration but NOT the per-dose milligram value or the week-by-week schedule, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are the literal VERIFY (never invented). ISMP tall-man (vinCRIStine); 2 mg per-dose cap retained as a standard safety guard. Infant/low-BSA dosing uses body-weight (30-Rule) or BSA-banded tables (lines 2086 to 2089).

drugs.name: Dactinomycin (actinomycin-D)

provenance.locator: Chemotherapy Regimens (WILMS-G): DD4A = 5 doses of dactinomycin (alternating with doxorubicin) over 24 weeks; EE4A = 7 doses over 18 weeks (lines 2028 to 2030)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC. DD4A specifies 5 doses of dactinomycin alternating with doxorubicin (EE4A: 7 doses). Per-dose milligram value and schedule are NOT printed, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are VERIFY. Reduce dactinomycin by 50% for 6 weeks after whole-lung/whole-abdomen irradiation to avoid radiation recall (line 2090); dactinomycin held if patient is undergoing RT overlap. Veno-occlusive/sinusoidal-obstruction hepatopathy occurs most often after vincristine/dactinomycin (line 2080 to 2083).

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin

provenance.locator: Chemotherapy Regimens (WILMS-G): DD4A = 4 doses of doxorubicin, cumulative dose 150 mg/m2 over 24 weeks (line 2029); Principles of Chemotherapy toxicity/echocardiogram guidance (lines 2069 to 2073); dexrazoxane supportive care (lines 2093 to 2095)

drugs.notes: PEDIATRIC. DD4A specifies 4 doses of doxorubicin with a PLANNED CUMULATIVE dose of 150 mg/m2 (line 2029); the per-dose milligram value is not printed, so basis, dosePerUnit, and unit are VERIFY. DOXOrubicin is only in DD4A (and M/I/UH regimens), NOT in EE4A. ISMP tall-man (DOXOrubicin). Pediatric anthracycline stakes are higher (younger children, especially those assigned female at birth, are more susceptible to cardiotoxicity): echocardiogram before the first dose, before exceeding cumulative 200 mg/m2 (the warn threshold set here), and at end of treatment (line 2072). Dexrazoxane should be given before each doxorubicin dose if planned cumulative will exceed 150 mg/m2, at a 10:1 dexrazoxane:doxorubicin ratio (lines 2093 to 2095). Reduce doxorubicin 50% for 6 weeks after WLI/WAI (line 2090).

supportiveCare: EE4A (very-low/low-risk FHWT): vinCRIStine + Dactinomycin only, 13 + 7 doses over 18 weeks (line 2028). DD4A (standard/higher-risk FHWT): adds DOXOrubicin, 15 + 5 + 4 doses over 24 weeks with alternating dactinomycin/doxorubicin (line 2029). Adverse molecular markers (combined LOH 1p/16q, 1q gain) or slow lung-metastasis response escalate therapy to Regimen M (adds cyclophosphamide/etoposide; lines 2034 to 2037).

cycleLengthDays and cycles are VERIFY: EE4A and DD4A are week-based dose schedules (18 and 24 weeks respectively) and the source prints dose counts and total duration but not a fixed cycle length or per-dose day schedule; these must be resolved from a cited COG dosing source before activation.

doxorubicin (DD4A): dexrazoxane if planned cumulative >150 mg/m2 (10:1 ratio); echocardiogram before first dose, before cumulative 200 mg/m2, and at end of treatment; lower pediatric cardiotoxicity threshold.
dactinomycin/doxorubicin: reduce by 50% for 6 weeks after whole-lung or whole-abdomen irradiation (radiation recall).
G-CSF (filgrastim/pegfilgrastim): not necessary after EE4A, DD4A, or VAD, but consider for cyclophosphamide/etoposide-containing cycles in Regimen M and above (lines 2096 to 2098).
hepatopathy/sinusoidal-obstruction syndrome surveillance (most often after vincristine/dactinomycin).

monitoring: echocardiogram before first doxorubicin dose, before cumulative 200 mg/m2, and at end of treatment (DD4A)
liver function and clinical signs of sinusoidal-obstruction syndrome (abdominal distension, ascites, hepatomegaly, transaminase/bilirubin rise, thrombocytopenia)
coordination with radiation timing to avoid full-dose dactinomycin/doxorubicin during RT

doseModificationRules.condition: combined LOH at 1p and 16q, 1q gain, or slow/incomplete lung-metastasis response
doseModificationRules.text: Escalate therapy (continue/switch to DD4A, or switch to Regimen M which adds cyclophosphamide/etoposide) per risk reassessment and clinical review (lines 2034 to 2037, 522 to 558).
Obtain echocardiogram before exceeding cumulative 200 mg/m2; give dexrazoxane if planned cumulative >150 mg/m2 (10:1 ratio); clinical review of cardiac function (lines 2072, 2093 to 2095).

doseModificationRules.condition: within 6 weeks after whole-lung or whole-abdomen irradiation
doseModificationRules.text: Reduce dactinomycin and doxorubicin doses by 50% to ameliorate radiation recall (line 2090).

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Wilms tumor (nephroblastoma) is a pediatric tumor; per-drug pediatric milligram doses for EE4A/DD4A are not printed in the provided adult extract, so regimen identity and dose scaffolding are grounded to the NCCN Wilms Tumor guideline layer

guideline.locator: Initial/Final Risk Assessment for FHWT (WILMS-F, lines 522 to 558); Chemotherapy Regimens (WILMS-G, lines 2027 to 2047); Principles of Chemotherapy toxicity/dose-modification/supportive-care (WILMS-G, lines 2063 to 2098); adjuvant timing (line 2019 to 2021)

provenanceNote: PEDIATRIC ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for Wilms tumor / nephroblastoma (StewardMD reference disease wilms_tumour). Regimen identity is grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Wilms Tumor (Nephroblastoma) v1.2026: Regimen EE4A = vinCRIStine + Dactinomycin (13 + 7 doses over 18 weeks) for very-low/low-risk favorable-histology WT, and Regimen DD4A = vinCRIStine + Dactinomycin + DOXOrubicin (15 + 5 + 4 doses over 24 weeks, doxorubicin cumulative 150 mg/m2) for standard/higher-risk favorable-histology WT (Chemotherapy Regimens WILMS-G, lines 2028 to 2029). Risk-directed assignment by histology (favorable vs anaplastic), stage, tumor weight, age, lung-metastasis response, and molecular markers - combined LOH at 1p and 16q, 1q gain, and 11p15 LOH/LOI - is grounded to the FHWT risk table (WILMS-F, lines 522 to 558) and biomarker-intensification updates (lines 153, 184, 226 to 227). The source prints dose COUNTS, total durations, and the doxorubicin planned cumulative (150 mg/m2), but does NOT print per-dose milligram values or a fixed cycle length, so every drug basis/dosePerUnit/unit plus cycleLengthDays and cycles are set to the literal VERIFY and listed in verifyFields rather than invented. Pediatric anthracycline safety is retained: echocardiogram before the first doxorubicin dose, before cumulative 200 mg/m2 (the warn threshold), and at end of treatment; dexrazoxane before each dose when planned cumulative exceeds 150 mg/m2 at a 10:1 ratio; 50% reduction of dactinomycin/doxorubicin for 6 weeks after whole-lung/whole-abdomen irradiation; and sinusoidal-obstruction hepatopathy surveillance (lines 2069 to 2095). ISMP tall-man applied (vinCRIStine 2 mg cap, DOXOrubicin). Status is DRAFT with unresolved VERIFY fields. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
